header:
Date: 2027-08-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Thompson (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Dr. Lena Ruiz (Aventra CTO), Marcus Chen (Aventra Head of Platform), Aisha Bello (Aventra SRE), Tom Keller (Aventra Procurement)
summary: Follow-up bridge to contain a recent eviction spike that caused long-tail latency for critical inference routes. We validated preliminary root cause hypotheses (KV cache TTL misalignment + aggressive horizontal autoscaler), agreed immediate mitigations (temp dedicated pool, raise cache TTL, backpressure/circuit breaker), and scheduled synthetic replay and soak tests. Action items assigned for logs, replay config, and SLA language updates.
topics: short-term mitigations (dedicated pool, TTL changes, circuit breaker)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (AE): ok everyone on the call? great thanks for jumping in, uh this is a short follow up from last nights incident - we're going to run through what we saw and what we think fixed it so far.
[00:18] Dr. Ruiz (CTO): yep I can hear you. we were pretty rattled by the tail latencies, customers seeing 5-10s spikes intermittently which is not acceptable.
[00:30] Diego (SE): quick context — we pulled trace samples and the dominant pattern we saw was repeated KV cache evictions at the model host layer, subsequent cache miss thrash, and then the continuous batching queue backed up, so token latencies cascaded.
[00:48] Marcus (Head of Platform): just to be clear, is this the redis layer TTL? we have a two-tier cache: local in-memory KV cache and redis as a backing store. our ops team only changed TTLs last month.
[01:02] Aisha (SRE): yeah we moved some TTLs to 60s to reduce memory footprint — that change lines up with the window where the spike started.
[01:10] Diego (SE): right and the autoscaler config reacts to CPU usage in a way that caused pod churn under burst. pods that started up had cold model caches; the request routing didn't prefer warm nodes so requests were shunting to cold caches. combined with smaller TTLs that caused a lot of eviction noise.
[01:29] Dr. Ruiz: that matches our post-incident notes. what are the immediate actions we can take to stop the next spike?
[01:36] Maya: we proposed three immediate mitigations: 1) provision a temporary dedicated pool (short-term reserved capacity) for the hot routes; 2) increase KV cache TTLs back to previous baseline and switch on a slightly more aggressive LRU hold for small keys; 3) enable a circuit breaker on the long-poll route so downstream clients get a fast fail rather than pile into the queue.
[01:58] Tom (Procurement): will the dedicated pool cost extra? we need a ballpark to sign off over the weekend.
[02:05] Maya: yes it'll be a short-term bump, we can provide an estimate — Diego we should capture expected token/min delta and cost estimate.
[02:12] Diego: noted, I'll run the numbers and share a 72-hour cost estimate.
[02:17] Aisha: one question — are we confident this is purely a cache TTL thing? there were some OOMs the same night.
[02:24] Diego: good call — we saw pod restarts tied to out-of-memory in one node, but root cause appears to be reactive scaling increasing memory pressure because each new pod loaded model kernels and warmed kvs simultaneously. so it's the interaction between scaling and small TTL.
[02:40] Marcus: so longer term we need smarter warmup and routing, maybe a pre-warm job or prefer-warm routing.
[02:47] Diego: exactly — prefetch, plus a routing policy that prefers nodes with a KV warmness score. that's medium-term. short term the dedicated pool prevents churn on the hot path.
[02:58] Dr. Ruiz: how fast can you stand up that pool?
[03:01] Maya: we can provision a weekend pool tonight; need your sign-off and the expected qps shape.
[03:07] Aisha: we can share load histograms by EOD.
[03:10] Maya: great.
[03:12] [00:03:12] Diego: for the circuit breaker we recommend a 1500ms soft-fail threshold for that route while the pool is active, with automatic rollback if error rates go up. it's a protection to keep the queue from backing up.
[03:26] Dr. Ruiz: wont that surface more client errors? our product team will scream.
[03:30] Priya (CSM): it will, but it's preferable to long tail latency and timeouts for end users — we can coordinate comms and a temporary user-facing message explaining degraded throughput.
[03:40] Marcus: ok but we need clear metrics to determine success. what's the runbook look like?
[03:46] Diego: short runbook: 1) provision dedicated pool with X GPUs and restrict hot routes; 2) bump KV TTLs from 60s to 600s for hot keys and change LRU hold; 3) enable circuit breaker at 1500ms and set error budget alert; 4) run synthetic replay for 4 hours with captured traffic shape; 5) observe p95/p99 and token cost delta.
[04:08] Aisha: can you record the exact kernel flags or quantization profile you use when provisioning the pool? we had a mismatch in kernel build last time.
[04:15] Diego: yes — I'll attach build flags and quant profile. we discovered one of the model variants was running a non-quantized path which increased memory by ~20%.
[04:24] Dr. Ruiz: that would explain the OOMs.
[04:27] Maya: noted — Diego add that to action items.
[04:31] [00:04:31] Aisha: on the observability side we need per-token tracing to correlate cache miss spikes to caller request ids; currently traces are sampled 1% and that's not enough.
[04:43] Diego: we can temporarily raise trace sampling to 10% during the soak and then pull full cold-start traces. there will be a storage cost but it's finite.
[04:51] Marcus: procurement question — our legal team flagged the need for an emergency clause if we require dedicated capacity; Tom (procurement) is on the call.
[04:59] Tom: yes can we get a short-term contract addendum for weekend capacity and explicit rollback terms?
[05:05] Maya: absolutely, I'll have a templated addendum sent for signature; Priya will update CRM.
[05:11] [00:05:11] Dr. Ruiz: ok let's talk about verification — what metrics will you provide to prove it's fixed?
[05:16] Diego: p50, p95, p99 latency for the hot route; cache hit ratio, cold-start rate, pod churn rate, and model memory usage. we'll provide baseline vs soak test graphs.
[05:27] Aisha: and heap/oom patterns per node.
[05:29] Diego: right.
[05:31] Maya: to be pragmatic — we'll do a staged run: provision the pool, bump TTLs, enable circuit breaker, then start 4-hour synthetic replay with elevated sampling. during the first hour we watch for regressions, if stable we continue soak.
[05:47] Dr. Ruiz: if regressions appear do we have automatic rollback?
[05:50] Diego: yes we'll script config rollback and fallback routing to a safe smaller model variant.
[05:56] Marcus: how about long-term: warmup, admission control, and routing by warmness — what's the timeline?
[06:02] Diego: engineering estimate: 6-8 weeks for warmness routing and prefetching, 2-3 sprints to add admission control and improved backpressure signals. we'll prepare a roadmap doc.
[06:12] Priya: we'll add that to the joint roadmap and track milestones.
[06:16] [00:06:16] Tom: procurement — any discount for a committed reserved block if we sign for 3 months?
[06:22] Maya: yes we can build a short reserved commitment with scaled discounts; we'll model for your expected token-mins.
[06:28] Dr. Ruiz: ok thanks. one more thing — security: we need the private-deploy checklist and KMS integration notes before we consider moving critical routes to private.
[06:38] Maya: I'll send the private-deploy checklist and KMS integration guide after the call.
[06:42] Diego: and for the replay we'll need the exact request shapes and any non-deterministic prompts sanitized.
[06:48] Aisha: we'll sanitize and ship logs to the secure S3 bucket you provided.
[06:52] [00:06:52] Diego: last technical point — we saw a small percentage of requests hit a non-quantized codepath; we want to lock model variants to a verified quantized image for the hot routes to reduce memory.
[07:04] Marcus: please include that in the runbook.
[07:07] Diego: done.
[07:09] Maya: ok let's recap and owners. Diego will run replay and share cost, Aisha will send eviction traces, Priya will update CRM and SLA, Maya will send contract addendum and security docs. any blockers?
[07:21] Dr. Ruiz: none from our side, appreciate quick turnaround.
[07:24] Tom: we'll review addendum and try to sign same day.
[07:27] Maya: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email with the exact timestamps for the soak and the invite for the deep dive.
[07:34] [End of recording]
